coverage.checklistItem: Record the authorized targets, accounts, test window, contacts, and prohibited actions.
coverage.note: Authorization and prohibited actions must come from the owner of the system.

coverage.checklistItem: Identify sensitive data, privileged functions, public entry points, and likely abuse cases.
coverage.note: The public runner cannot infer business sensitivity or likely abuse cases.

coverage.checklistItem: Choose and record the review sections based on exposure, data sensitivity, transactions, user privileges, and the evidence available.
coverage.note: Scope selection requires project context and human judgment.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm the canonical site loads over HTTPS with a certificate that is trusted, valid for the hostname, and within its validity dates.
coverage.note: The browser verifies the loaded URL and accepted certificate; the reviewer still confirms that the URL is canonical.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm plain HTTP redirects to the canonical HTTPS URL without a downgrade or redirect loop.
coverage.note: The runner follows a bounded redirect chain on the authorized hostname; the reviewer confirms the final URL is canonical.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm production uses supported TLS protocols and cryptography and does not accept deprecated options.
coverage.note: The runner records only the protocol negotiated for this request and does not enumerate every accepted protocol or cipher.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm pages, subresources, and form actions do not use insecure HTTP where HTTPS is required.
coverage.note: The runner checks the rendered page and observed requests, not every page or application state.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm production HTTPS responses send an HSTS policy with the project-approved duration and domain scope.
coverage.note: The runner records the header and active max-age; the reviewer decides the approved duration and subdomain scope.

coverage.checklistItem: Review the enforced Content Security Policy and record missing, invalid, or unnecessarily broad directives.
coverage.note: The runner detects a missing policy and a small set of broad directives; application-specific policy review remains manual.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm responses restrict framing, prevent content-type sniffing, and use an appropriate referrer policy.
coverage.note: The runner checks the main document response; policy appropriateness and other response types require review.

coverage.checklistItem: Review cookies issued by public pages and confirm their `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, and `SameSite` settings match their purpose.
coverage.note: The runner records cookie names and attributes without values; intended purpose and cookies from other states require review.

coverage.checklistItem: Review CORS headers on sampled public responses and confirm they grant access only to intended origins, methods, headers, and credentials.
coverage.note: The runner records CORS headers on the main response and flags one invalid combination; it does not send active cross-origin probes.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm normal responses and approved error pages do not reveal stack traces, debug details, private data, or unnecessary software versions.
coverage.note: The runner checks selected response headers and browser-error counts on one normal page; approved error pages and response bodies require manual review.

coverage.checklistItem: Recommended: publish a current `/.well-known/security.txt` file when the organization accepts vulnerability reports.
coverage.note: The runner checks the conventional file on the authorized origin; the organization decides whether it is applicable and whether the contact process works.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm runtimes, frameworks, plugins, and dependencies are supported and do not have unresolved vulnerabilities that exceed the project's risk tolerance.
coverage.note: This requires source, inventory, advisory, and project risk evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Scan the release for exposed secrets and unsafe production configuration without copying secret values into the review evidence.
coverage.note: Use approved source and secret-scanning tools; the public runner does not inspect the release package.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm production debug features and unused services are disabled and known management, diagnostic, backup, and storage endpoints are appropriately restricted.
coverage.note: This requires known configuration and endpoints; the runner does not enumerate routes or services.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm authorization for protected pages, data, files, object identifiers, and actions is enforced on the server.
coverage.note: Authorization testing requires approved accounts, roles, data, and actions.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm untrusted input is validated on the server and output is encoded or sanitized for the context where it is used.
coverage.note: A CSP observation does not prove input validation or contextual output handling.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm file uploads restrict type, size, storage location, execution, and access when uploads are supported.
coverage.note: Upload controls require authorized source and workflow testing.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm state-changing requests have appropriate CSRF protection and important workflows resist tampering, skipped steps, and duplicate actions.
coverage.note: The public runner does not submit forms or modify application state.

coverage.checklistItem: Review applicable APIs, webhooks, redirects, parsers, templates, and server-side requests for injection, unsafe destinations, and unintended access.
coverage.note: This requires project-specific source and authorized integration testing.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm the application uses supported cryptographic libraries and protocols and does not implement custom cryptography.
coverage.note: Negotiated browser TLS does not establish how the application implements cryptography.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm sensitive data and private files are protected in storage, caches, logs, exports, backups, and management tools.
coverage.note: This requires data-flow, storage, access, and operational evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Using approved test accounts, test sign-in, sign-out, account recovery, password changes, and multifactor authentication when supported.
coverage.note: Credentials and authenticated actions require explicit approval and project-specific interaction.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm roles, privileged accounts, and service accounts have only the access they require.
coverage.note: Role design and account access require administrative evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Test representative roles and object identifiers to confirm users cannot access another user's data or perform privileged actions.
coverage.note: Cross-role authorization testing requires explicit authorization, test accounts, and safe test data.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm sessions rotate when privilege changes, expire as intended, become invalid after sign-out, and use appropriately protected cookies.
coverage.note: Public cookie observations do not establish authenticated session behavior.

coverage.checklistItem: Test important workflows for unauthorized changes, skipped steps, repeated submissions, and failures that expose data or bypass controls.
coverage.note: State-changing workflow tests are project-specific and require explicit authorization.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm important security events are logged and that logs do not contain secrets.
coverage.note: Log coverage and contents require access to the approved logging system.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm that meaningful alerts reach an owner.
coverage.note: Alert routing and ownership require operational evidence or an approved test.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm emergency patching, vulnerability reports, incident response, and credential rotation have owners and usable procedures.
coverage.note: Operational ownership and procedure usability require human review.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm backups are protected and restoration has been tested.
coverage.note: Backup protection and restoration require operational evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Review automated findings manually before treating them as confirmed issues.
coverage.note: The evidence package supplies observations; a reviewer must confirm their context and impact.

coverage.checklistItem: Retest fixes and look for the same problem in shared code or related endpoints.
coverage.note: Retesting depends on a changed release and the affected shared code or endpoints.

coverage.checklistItem: Record evidence, untested areas, accepted risks, follow-up work, owners, and any required ASVS mapping.
coverage.note: The package records public evidence and automation limits; owners, accepted risk, follow-up, and ASVS mapping require human decisions.
